muscle_engagement.note: Primary mover for shoulder adduction and extension.
Assists lats in shoulder extension and adduction.
Assists in scapular depression and stabilization.
Assists in elbow flexion. Generally lower activation compared to underhand chin-up (Youdas et al. 2010).

muscle_engagement.note: Strongly activated, mostly via shoulder extension.
Significantly higher activation than overhand pull-ups due to supinated grip (Youdas et al. 2010).

muscle_engagement.note: Maintains isometric spinal extension (Fenwick et al. 2009).

Elbow flexor; assists elbow flexion during the pulling phase. Listed because the exercise's joint_actions include elbow flexion, and an action with no muscle assigned to produce it is a data inconsistency.

engagement_caveat: Heavy reliance on erector spinae for stabilization can be a limiting factor compared to chest-supported rows.
source_refs: Fenwick et al., Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 2009;23(2):350-358 (Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness); DOI: 10.1519/JSC.0b013e3181942019

Lusk et al., Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 2010;24(7):1895-1900 (Grip width and forearm orientation effects on muscle activity during the lat pull-down); DOI: 10.1519/JSC.0b013e3181ddb0ab

muscle_engagement.note: Elbow flexor; assists elbow flexion during the pulling phase. Listed because the exercise's joint_actions include elbow flexion, and an action with no muscle assigned to produce it is a data inconsistency.
Assists, but less than anterior in standard grip.

Contracts isometrically to hold the trunk upright (spinal extensors). Note: resisting lumbar hyperextension under an overhead load is anti-extension work performed by the abdominal wall, not by erector spinae.

source_refs: Saeterbakken et al., Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 2013;27(7):1824-1831 (Effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses); DOI: 10.1519/JSC.0b013e318276b873
engagement_caveat: Standing (vs seated) increases trunk stabiliser demand. Erector spinae holds the trunk upright; the abdominal wall resists the lumbar hyperextension that an overhead load encourages. Abdominal engagement is not itemised here because this dataset has no sourced EMG values for it in this exercise.

muscle_engagement.note: Highly targets the lateral deltoid in frontal or scapular plane.

source_refs: Coratella et al., International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 2020;17(17):6015 (An Electromyographic Analysis of Lateral Raise Variations and Frontal Raise in Competitive Bodybuilders); DOI: 10.3390/ijerph17176015

engagement_caveat: Often considered redundant if the training program already includes significant pressing (bench press, shoulder press), which heavily targets the anterior deltoid.

muscle_engagement.note: Assists in horizontal abduction and external rotation.

source_refs: Franke et al., Journal of Sports Medicine and Physical Fitness 2015;55(7-8):714-721 (Analysis of anterior, middle and posterior deltoid activation...)

muscle_engagement.note: Primary knee extensors. High activation compared to other leg exercises.
Primary hip extensor, heavily activated at depth (Caterisano et al. 2002).
Less activated than vasti due to biarticular nature (shortening at hip, lengthening at knee).
Acts to stabilize the knee, relatively low activation as prime movers in squats due to biarticular paradox.
Important hip extensor, especially at the bottom of the squat.

engagement_caveat: Hamstrings are poorly stimulated for hypertrophy during squats (Kubo et al. 2019). Squats are primarily a quad/glute exercise.
source_refs: Kubo et al., European Journal of Applied Physiology 2019;119(9):1933-1942 (Effects of squat training with different depths on lower limb muscle volumes); DOI: 10.1007/s00421-019-04181-y
Caterisano et al., Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 2002;16(3):428-432 (The effect of back squat depth on the EMG activity); DOI: 10.1519/00124278-200208000-00014

muscle_engagement.note: Phase-dependent synergist/dynamic stabilizer; contribution varies throughout the lift.
Maintains isometric spinal extension, often the limiting factor.
Provides knee extension to lift off the floor.

source_refs: Martin-Fuentes et al., PLoS One 2020;15(2):e0229507 (Electromyographic activity in deadlift exercise and its variants. A systematic review); DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0229507

muscle_engagement.note: Hip extension contribution varies with foot placement (higher feet = more glutes/hamstrings).
Highly activated compared to squats due to hip being flexed and stable.
Seated version places hamstrings at a longer muscle length, enhancing hypertrophy (Maeo et al. 2021).

engagement_caveat: Seated leg curl provides greater hypertrophy for hamstrings than prone leg curl due to the stretch-mediated hypertrophy effect (Maeo et al. 2021).
source_refs: Maeo et al., Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise 2021;53(4):825-837 (Greater Hamstrings Muscle Hypertrophy but Similar Damage Protection after Training at Long versus Short Muscle Lengths); DOI: 10.1249/MSS.0000000000002523

muscle_engagement.note: High peak EMG activation at end-range of hip extension.
Contributes to hip extension but reduced efficacy due to bent knees (active insufficiency).

engagement_caveat: Despite higher EMG activation than squats in some studies (Contreras et al. 2015), recent matched-volume trials (Plotkin et al. 2023) show similar gluteal hypertrophy outcomes between squats and hip thrusts. The 'activation gap' does not necessarily translate to a 'growth gap'.
source_refs: Plotkin et al., Frontiers in Physiology 2023;14:1279170 (Hip thrust and back squat training elicit similar gluteus muscle hypertrophy...); DOI: 10.3389/fphys.2023.1279170
Contreras et al., Journal of Applied Biomechanics 2015;31(6):452-458; DOI: 10.1123/jab.2014-0301

muscle_engagement.note: Primary hip flexor initiating the leg raise.
Assists in hip flexion, particularly with straight legs.
Acts isometrically to maintain posterior pelvic tilt and prevent lumbar extension. Becomes a prime mover only if actively curling the pelvis upward.
Assists in maintaining pelvic position and resisting extension.

engagement_caveat: Two distinct variants. Base version (shown here): straight-leg raise driven by hip flexors, with the abdominals working isometrically to hold posterior pelvic tilt and prevent lumbar extension. Pelvic-curl variant: a deliberate posterior pelvic tilt/spinal flexion is added, and rectus abdominis then becomes a prime mover for that component. Do not present this exercise as isolating the 'lower abs' -- that regional distinction is not supported. Hanging also imposes an isometric shoulder-girdle and grip demand; that is a stabilisation requirement, not a joint action of the exercise, and the muscles responsible are not itemised here.

muscle_engagement.note: Strong elbow flexor active in all forearm positions.

engagement_caveat: Because the long head of the biceps brachii crosses the shoulder joint, performing curls with the shoulder in extension (such as on an incline bench) places the muscle at a longer length, which can lead to distinct muscle growth adaptations. Recent studies suggest incline curls may promote greater proximal biceps thickness compared to preacher curls.
source_refs: Oliveira et al., Journal of Sports Science & Medicine 2009;8(1):24-29 (Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls)
International Journal of Sports Medicine 2025 (Distinct muscle growth and strength adaptations after preacher and incline biceps curl); DOI: 10.1055/a-2517-0509

muscle_engagement.note: Strong elbow flexor active in all forearm positions.
Still active, but neutral grip shifts relative emphasis toward brachioradialis.

engagement_caveat: Because the long head of the triceps brachii crosses the shoulder joint, performing elbow extension with the shoulder flexed (overhead position) places the long head in a lengthened state. Studies show this leads to substantially greater triceps hypertrophy compared to neutral-arm pushdowns.
source_refs: Maeo et al., European Journal of Sport Science 2023;23(7):1214-1226 (Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position); DOI: 10.1080/17461391.2022.2100279
